newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee exports rise in first 96/97 quarter.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee exports rise in first 96/97 quarter.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports rose in the first quarter of 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) compared to the same period in the previous year, the state-owned Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Thursday.

In a report for December, UCDA said some 1,291,096 60-kg bags of coffee were sold in October-December, valued at $95.2 million compared to 795,502 bags valued at $88 million in the same period the previous year.
In December 1996, a revised total of 514,394 bags valued at $35.85 million were shipped, up from 353,960 bags worth $32.57 million realised in the month of November.

Robusta Screen 15 (Standard) dominated the market and accounted for 63.5 percent of exports. Over 90 percent of the sales were contracted by private exporters of whom 14 accounted for 80 percent of the market share.

Local prices for FAQ (fair average quality) were 700 to 900 shillings per kg while lower quality kiboko ranged between 350 and 400 shillings per kg. Arabica parchment prices oscillated between 1,150 and 1,250 shillings per kg.
The December local prices were lower compared to 1995 in line with international trends at the time.
December export volume rose by 17.9 percent. The export unit value in the month of December 1996 fell to $1.16 per kg from $1.24 per kg in the previous month.

UCDA said the rise in exports over the period was attributable to high levels of closing stocks reported at the end of 1995/96. However, the volumes were also up because the central and eastern coffee districts were at their peak.
In the opening of this quarter, exporters took advantage of high availability of coffee in the internal market to fulfil contractual needs which had remained pending in 1995/96.

Front loading of stocks on the market by farmers in a bid to avoid financial losses after seeing the persistent fall in global prices and need for money to spend over Christmas were also responsible for higher exports, UCDA said.

Sales increased in December by some 183 percent from the preceeding month despite relatively lower international markets. The heavy selling activity was attributed to stiff competition associated with free market systems and Christmas spending.
